execution_policy: Every command below names a future unimplemented runner. MUST NOT RUN. These designs authorize no harness creation, helper qualification, service installation, GDB/MCP/emulator use, target execution, or runtime attempt.

baseline.interpretation: The baseline does not qualify the installed service, actual helper integration, complete offline controller path, or live Ready. No prior gate is rerun by this card set.

decision.first_independently_useful_repair: Add a caller-owned service creation lease, then qualify actual copied service methods with a denied real subprocess factory. The caller knows owner_id before start; the service retains process ownership through confirmed exit or UNRESOLVED.

proposed_additive_api.start: start_owned_session(owner_id, binary, args, cwd) -> lease state; owner_id is caller-generated and single-use for one fixed attempt; register synchronously before first spawn await. Preserve the manager fixed GDB launch (gdb --interpreter=mi2 --quiet) and its existing binary,args,cwd authority; do not add executable, argv, or env launch controls
proposed_additive_api.owned_command: exec_owned_session(owner_id, session_id, command_id, command, budget_ms) -> {owner_id, session_id, command_id, text, mi_result, mi_error, stop_record}; bind the parsed MI result/error and any stop record to that serialized command; absent, ambiguous, or unmatched stop records remain UNKNOWN
proposed_additive_api.compatibility: Keep start_session, stop_session, exec_command and batch_commands signatures and string/batch response schemas unchanged. New owned methods are separately named and additive; no install or deployment is authorized.
owner_rules: Owner token is single-use for one fixed attempt.
Same token and identical launch tuple returns the existing lease; never spawn a second process.
Same token with a changed launch tuple returns OWNER_CONFLICT without spawn.
Stop before a delayed start creates CANCELLED_BEFORE_START tombstone; later start rejects without spawn.
EXITED requires proc.wait() to return a return code. Otherwise retain the lease and report UNRESOLVED.

decision.unresolved_external_proof: A client Promise.race, controller virtual clock, relative budget, or copied-source fake cannot prove MCP transport cancellation/deadline behavior. Real service integration remains blocked until separately authorized deployment and an end-to-end transport proof.
decision.clock_contract: Service and caller use separate monotonic clock domains. Never compare their absolute values. A passed relative budget does not prove cancellation of the remote operation.

fixture_and_controls.controlled_state: The future runner injects a factory into the actual copied service module. Its default/denial factory raises immediately if a real subprocess launch is attempted. Controlled fake stdin/stdout, drain gates, wait/terminate/kill results, owner tokens, and launch tuples are local to one invocation.
good_cases: Start is paused after fake process creation and before the start response. stop_session_by_owner with the pre-known token requests cleanup; the same process remains owned until fake wait returns its exact return code.
Repeat start with the same owner and identical launch tuple; expected spawn count remains exactly 1 and both calls observe one lease.

Exercise serialized send with lock wait, stdin write/drain, and response collection under one proposed 1000 ms service-monotonic budget; a successful response within budget is accepted only when each stage shares that deadline.
broken_controls: Cancel owner before delayed start; expect CANCELLED_BEFORE_START and spawn count exactly 0 after the later start request.
Reuse owner with a different launch tuple; expect OWNER_CONFLICT and no additional spawn.
Cancel or fail startup while banner/setup is pending after spawn; expect STOP_REQUESTED then EXITED only after fake wait returns, never an unowned process.

Block drain beyond the same 1000 ms deadline; expect deadline failure, no next command admission, and retained UNRESOLVED ownership until stop/wait resolves. Do not assert that cancelling drain alone stops the transport.

Make close share one 7000 ms absolute service-monotonic deadline across quit write/drain, graceful wait capped at 3000 ms, terminate wait capped at 2000 ms, kill, and final wait. Final wait receives only remaining time. Return EXITED only after fake wait returns; suppress final wait completion and expect UNRESOLVED plus a retained registry entry/task.
Repeat stop; expect an idempotent terminal/ongoing state and no second spawn or duplicate kill.

independent_expected_values.close_deadline_scope: One absolute service-monotonic deadline from close entry covers quit write/drain, graceful wait, terminate wait, kill and final wait. Graceful/terminate caps are at most 3000/2000 ms; final wait gets only remaining time. If write/drain or final wait consumes the deadline, retain the operation task and owner lease as UNRESOLVED.
independent_expected_values.runtime_cleanup_partition: UNPROVEN: do not claim the 7000 ms service close fits the controller 8000 ms reserve until child/GDB/finalization partition or an independent concurrency contract is frozen.
independent_expected_values.exit_truth: EXITED iff wait() returned a return code; otherwise UNRESOLVED and retained
independent_expected_values.tolerance: Exact counts and states; no timing tolerance beyond a single service-monotonic deadline. Phase wall-clock maximum is 60000 ms.

python_bridge_blocker.reason: controller-v3.js is JavaScript, while the pinned guard, window, observer and analysis functions are Python. No in-process bridge is frozen; the no-subprocess containment therefore cannot call the actual Python functions from that controller.
python_bridge_blocker.candidate_future_contract: A separately approved bounded Python worker/file+JSON protocol or another reviewed architecture. Candidate boundary: controller-v3.js writes one request.json under its unique attempt directory with owner_id, attempt_id, input artifact paths and a relative budget; it starts exactly one fixed python3 -B invocation of the copied python-admission/analysis.py worker; that worker imports/calls only the actual copied functions, writes one result.json atomically with matching owner_id/attempt_id and a terminal status, then exits. Request/result paths must remain inside the attempt directory.
python_bridge_blocker.ownership_deadlines_exit: The JS caller creates a single-use owner token before worker creation, owns the direct child, records PID/start_ticks, and requires proc.wait() returncode 0 plus matching complete result.json for worker success. One outer controller monotonic deadline covers worker, validation and finalization; pass only relative remaining budget, never compare JS/Python absolute clock values. Timeout cleanup uses one caller-local deadline; termination signal alone is not exit proof, and missing final wait returncode leaves the child UNRESOLVED with evidence retained. The existing 52/8 R-I work/cleanup split remains unproven.
python_bridge_blocker.containment: If later approved, the controlled local Python worker is the sole allowlisted child process; deny all other subprocesses, network, GDB/MCP construction and XRoar/guest launches. Expected external service calls and target launches are exactly zero. No worker command or launch is authorized now.
